title: The Forgotten Sigil
premise: Noor Nystrom, a mercenary whose god fell silent seven years ago, scrapes by selling outlawed charms in the free city of Vell until a child named Sef arrives at his door speaking the First Tongue — the language of the covenant that once bound gods, mortals, and the land itself. Hunted by the usurper Kaelen Voss's witch-finders and betrayed by old comrades, Noor gathers a ragged found family: a disgraced inquisitor, a smuggler priestess, and Sef himself, who may be the covenant's living key. To end the usurper's conquest, Noor must journey to the drowned shrine where his god went silent and reforge the broken sigil at the cost of his own name and memory. In the climax he sacrifices his past to bind the realms anew; the armies break before the free cities, and Noor, nameless but not alone, begins again among the people who refuse to forget him.
about_author: Jonah Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-formulae before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about broken promises and the people stubborn enough to keep them anyway.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. We meet him hawking minor charms in Vell's night market while witch-finders patrol, establishing his silence-prayer ritual and his weary code: help no one too much. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A mud-caked boy, Sef, collapses on his doorstep speaking the First Tongue — words Noor's silent god once used. When witch-finders follow, Noor breaks his own rule and hides the child. Emotional beat: reluctant awakening of an old duty.

chapters.title: What the Witch-Finders Burn
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, fragmented and frightened. Through the child's eyes we see Voss's purge of magic-users and glimpse Sef's flight from a burned sanctuary. Noor interrogates him gently; the First Tongue responds to Noor's touch. Emotional beat: terror met with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Quit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Maren Solde, a former witch-finder who faked her death rather than burn children. She tracks Noor as a suspect, then saves them both from a raid. Emotional beat: two wary professionals recognizing each other's scars.

chapters.title: A Smuggler's Sacrament
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The trio seeks passage from Odile Ferran, a smuggler-priestess of the silenced pantheon who keeps forbidden rites alive in her ship's hold. She confirms Sef is a 'vessel-key' of the old covenant. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the first hint of found family.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Noor's POV. We learn how his mercenary company died holding a pass for a god who never answered, and why Noor blames himself — and the god. Emotional beat: grief reframed as betrayal; the wound the story must heal.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Edict
chapters.summary: Voss's POV (first antagonist view). Cold, rational, genuinely believing magic caused a past plague, he marches on the free cities and orders Sef taken alive. Emotional beat: dread; the enemy is principled, which is worse.

chapters.title: Salt and Old Words
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. At sea, Odile teaches Sef controlled use of the First Tongue; a storm nearly wrecks them until Sef's words calm it — revealing his power to everyone aboard. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by fear of what Sef is becoming.

chapters.title: The Toll of the Gray Strait
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A toll-keeper demands they surrender the child; Maren talks them through using her inquisitor credentials one last time, burning her old identity forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the past self, mirrored against Noor's coming choice.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Hand
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Her former partner Rask catches up, offering amnesty if she delivers Sef. She refuses; a fight kills two crew members and exposes their route. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve; loyalty chosen over survival.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Council
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The council of free cities refuses to believe the covenant can be reforged and plans mere fortification. Noor, humiliated, decides to go to the drowned shrine regardless — with only his new family volunteering. Emotional beat: defiance born of rejection.

chapters.title: Road of Hanged Kings
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Overland march through a canyon strung with the corpses of deposed rulers — Voss's warning. Ambush by deserters; Sef speaks a word that spares them, unsettling even Noor. Emotional beat: the cost of mercy, and awe at Sef's growth.

chapters.title: The Shrine Beneath the Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They reach the drowned shrine where Noor's company died. He descends alone and finds not a dead god but a wounded one, its voice stolen by the severed sigil. Emotional beat: revelation — the god never abandoned him; the covenant was sabotaged.

chapters.title: Who Cut the Cord
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Researching in the shrine's flooded archive, she discovers Voss's order predates his crusade: he cut the sigil years ago to seize divine power for himself. Emotional beat: righteous fury; justice now has a target.

chapters.title: Rask's Bargain
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Rask returns with an army detachment, offering Sef's life for the rest. Odile takes a mortal wound covering the escape into the shrine's deep tunnels. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the family pays its first blood price.

chapters.title: Dying Light, Dying Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, final hours. In the tunnels she passes her rites and her ship's keys to Sef, making him heir to something worth keeping. Emotional beat: transmission of faith; found family formalized in loss.

chapters.title: The Sigil Reforged
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the shrine's heart, reforging requires a mortal name given freely. Noor speaks his own name into the molten sigil, forgetting himself even as the god's voice returns through him. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-erasure — the theme's price made literal.

chapters.title: Armies at the Walls
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. His host reaches the free cities' walls as the sky changes; the reforged covenant stirs the land itself against him. His certainty cracks when his stolen power begins to answer to the true sigil instead. Emotional beat: the usurper's unraveling.

chapters.title: The Battle of Broken Banners
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Sef, channeling the renewed covenant, unbinds Voss's stolen power mid-battle; Maren duels Rask; the free cities rally. Voss falls not to a sword but to his own severed oaths turning on him. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice outside the law fulfilled.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Counting costs: Odile buried at sea, the city scarred, magic decriminalized but mistrusted. Maren declines a council seat, choosing to guard Sef instead. Emotional beat: weary gratitude; rebuilding begins with people, not institutions.

chapters.title: The Nameless Man
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, sparse and strange. He remembers nothing of himself but recognizes kindness when it's offered. Sef patiently retells him his own story, and the returned god whispers that names can be earned twice. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope; identity as gift rather than possession.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Sef's POV, closing mirror of chapter 2. On the rebuilt doorstep where he first arrived, Sef teaches the nameless man his first word in the First Tongue — 'home.' The covenant holds; the family remains. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; the cycle turned to blessing.
